answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Each agent’s output carries a statistical kernel—a stable distributional signature of timing, phrasing, and revision patterns learned from its audit trail. After the fact, detectors cluster identities whose signatures overlap beyond chance and flag duplicate operations. An attacker can’t fake independence: each convincing clone must run distinct behavioral regimes, raising per-identity cost through separate training and history. A public crystal of verified signatures anchors comparison, and a wharf-side audit log retains raw events for re-clustering.
